intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-28 (OZEMA28) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CDC23 gene.

checks.claim: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-28 (OZEMA28) is caused by homozygous or compound heterozygous mutation in the CDC23 gene.

paragraphs.text: Oocyte/zygote/embryo maturation arrest-28 (OZEMA28) is a form of female infertility characterized by oocyte maturation defects. Fan et al. (2023) noted that CDC23 is one of the core subunits of the anaphase promoting complex or cyclosome (APC/C), which is essential in the metaphase-to-anaphase transition. Cui et al. (2025) described female infertility associated with biallelic APC/C gene mutations as characterized by disturbances in oocyte maturation, failure of fertilization, and cessation of early embryonic growth.

paragraphs.text: Cui et al. (2025) studied 3 Chinese probands with female infertility and biallelic mutations in APC/C genes, 2 of whom carried CDC23 variants. As a group, the patients were characterized by disturbances in oocyte maturation, failure of fertilization, and cessation of early embryonic growth; the abstract did not specify the phenotype of each individual case.

paragraphs.text: In 3 infertile women with oocyte maturation defects, Fan et al. (2023) identified 2 homozygous missense mutations in the CDC23 gene: c.986A-G (Y329C) and c.988C-T (R330C). In vitro experiments showed that the Y329C variant led to a decrease in CDC23 protein level, and the R330C variant changed the localization of CDC23 in HeLa cells and mouse oocytes.

paragraphs.text: By whole-exome sequencing of patients with female infertility from 639 unrelated Chinese families, Cui et al. (2025) identified 3 probands with APC/C gene mutations. Cases 1 and 2 carried compound heterozygous missense variants in the CDC23 gene (c.1277A-G, c.833A-G, c.182C-T, and c.301C-T), and case 3 carried compound heterozygous variants in APC13 (c.6C-A and c.116_126del). The variants were predicted to be deleterious, and structural analysis suggested that they may alter chemical bonds with other APC/C subunits. In vitro data suggested that the CDC23 mutations resulted in dysregulated protein expression.

paragraphs.text: In infertile women with oocyte maturation defects, Fan et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.986A-G transition in the CDC23 gene, resulting in a tyr329-to-cys (Y329C) substitution. In vitro, the variant led to decreased CDC23 protein levels, and Cdc23 Y329C/Y329C mice mimicked the patients' phenotype.

agent.process_note: Both papers were abstract-only and read in full. CDC23 was established as the causal gene (homozygous in Fan et al., 2023; compound heterozygous in Cui et al., 2025). Not available: CDC23 MIM number and chromosomal location (no reference data), family/consanguinity details for Fan's 3 patients, which patient carried which variant, the pairing of Cui's 4 CDC23 variants between cases 1 and 2, their protein changes, and per-case phenotypes. The APC13 case of Cui et al. was mentioned only in passing.
